SSO Is the Gate on Enterprise Expansion

Three independent sources put the same missing capability in front of the same deals.

Author: Data Science  ·  2026-08-06  ·  Status: Draft  ·  Pairs with → "Enterprise SSO" PRD

TL;DR

Four HubSpot opportunities worth $1.4M are blocked on SAML SSO. Two Fireflies calls in the same period name it unprompted, and the support queue shows the same request from an existing enterprise account. Three independent source types, one capability.

OPPORTUNITY

Ship SAML SSO to unblock $1.4M of already-qualified enterprise pipeline.

Context. Enterprise deals reach security review and stop. This looks at what stops them and how consistently.

SIGNAL 1 — REVENUE (HUBSPOT)

Four opportunities stalled at the same stage.

Every stalled opportunity in the period carries the same blocker note. The amounts are as recorded on the opportunity, not modelled.

SIGNAL 2 — CUSTOMER VOICE (FIREFLIES)

Buyers raise it before we do.

In both calls the requirement is stated by the customer, unprompted, during security review.

Sales call

We can't roll this out past the pilot team without SAML.

Support

Our security review flagged the lack of SSO as a blocker for the wider rollout.

COMPETITIVE

Both alternatives ship it.

CapabilityVendor AVendor BUs
SAML SSOyesyesno
SCIM provisioningyesnono
What I extract: SSO is table stakes at this deal size, so its absence reads as a disqualifier rather than a gap.

CONVERGENCE

Three independent sources, one capability.

Revenue, customer voice and the competitive scan were gathered separately and name the same requirement. The agreement is strong; the sizing is not — $1.4M is pipeline, not booked revenue.
